title: Cap. IX Arg. 8: absolute reprobation not from foresight of actual sins makes God deal more rigidly with some men than with the very devils
pass_a_gloss: They who establish that God by his mere will, and not from foresight of actual sins and of final perseverance in the same, has reprobated certain ones, those establish that God deals far more rigidly with certain men than with the very devils: For whereas the devils are excluded from life on account of sins which by their own proper malice they committed, certain reprobated men are placed not on account of proper sins which in their persons they committed, but only considered as guilty by Divine imputation of the alien sin of Adam.
pass_b_english: Those who hold that God by mere will — not from foresight of actual sins and final perseverance in them — has reprobated some, thereby hold that God deals far more rigidly with certain men than with the very devils. For the devils are shut out of life for sins they committed by their own malice; yet some reprobated men are set not for sins done in their own persons, but only as guilty by divine imputation of Adam's alien sin.
source_text: Qui statuunt Deum mera sua voluntate, et non ex praevisione actualium peccatorum et finalis perseverantiae in iisdem, quosdam reprobasse, illi statuunt Deum longe rigidius agere cum hominibus quibusdam, quam cum ipsis diabolis: Cum enim diaboli excludantur a vita ob peccata quae propria sua malitia commiserunt, homines quidam reprobati ponuntur, non propter propria peccata quae in personis suis commiserunt, sed tantum considerati uti alieno peccato Adami ex imputatione Divina rei.
